transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-01
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 mins
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Daniel (Redwood SE), Sofia (Redwood DevAdv); Jordan (Aurora Eng Mgr), Priya (Backend), Ethan (Security)

Summary (auto): quick SDK walkthrough covering Python and TypeScript quickstarts, auth patterns (API keys vs SSO/service tokens), environment setup, and next steps to start a hosted pilot. A few side questions on Dedicated/VPC and audit logs.

Topics: SDK quickstart, auth & env, console walkthrough, Optimize suggestions, pilot plan, security notes

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll run through the SDK quickstarts, auth, and environment setup. Daniel will demo code examples.
[00:18] Jordan (Aurora): Thanks, Maya. We're excited - Priya will be implementing. Ethan's here for security questions.
[00:30] Daniel (Redwood SE): Cool, quick agenda: 1) Python quickstart, 2) TypeScript quickstart, 3) auth options, 4) Console + Optimize bits, then q&a. Sound good?
[00:40] Priya (Aurora): Yep, good. Our main constraints: low-latency for chat, p95 < 400ms, and data must not leave EU for certain flows.
[00:55] Daniel: Got it. We'll show hosted API first - easiest to get started - and then outline Dedicated and Private/VPC for residency.
[01:05] Sofia (Redwood): I'll drop the quickstart links in chat (repo + docs).
[01:15] Maya: Also I'll attach the pricing tiers and Dedicated commit options after the call.
[01:25] Daniel: Ok switching to screen, Python quickstart - pip install redwood-inference (note: package name in repo), then simple usage. Example:
[01:40] Daniel (reading): "from redwood import RedwoodClient
 client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY'))
 resp = client.generate(prompt='Hello from Aurora')"
[01:55] Priya: Quick question - how do you recommend storing the API key in production?
[02:05] Daniel: Good Q. Use your secret manager / env vars. For hosted, API keys are fine with RBAC and token rotation via Console. For Dedicated or Private, we recommend short-lived service tokens backed by your KMS; we'll share a pattern.
[02:20] Ethan (Aurora): Do you support SSO for service accounts?
[02:28] Maya: We integrate with SSO/SAML for the Console, and for service-to-service we usually do KMS-backed service tokens, or mTLS in private installs. We'll send the security doc covering audit logs, SOC2, ISO.
[02:40] Daniel: Now TypeScript quickstart - npm install @redwood/inference, then:
[02:50] Daniel (reading): "import Redwood from '@redwood/inference'
 const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY })
 const r = await client.chat.create({ messages: [...] })"
[03:05] Jordan: Any differences in behavior between SDKs?
[03:10] Daniel: No major differences, same API surface. Node SDK supports streaming reponses and function calls like the Python one. Some small differences in param names, but quickstart repo shows both.
[03:25] Priya: About streaming, we need token-by-token streaming to our websocket gateway - is that supported?
[03:35] Daniel: Yes, both SDKs have streaming; for large scale we show how to use continuous batching and prefix caching in Console. You'll configure batching windows and max tokens per batch.
[03:50] Priya: Who sets the batching? Us or Redwood?
[03:55] Sofia: The platform suggests defaults via Optimize, and you can override per-route in Console. For early pilot we can recommend config.
[04:10] Daniel: Quick note on auth examples in the repo - we include two flows: 1) simple API key in env (for dev), 2) service token with short TTL + KMS envelope (for prod).
[04:25] Ethan: We need audit logs and encryption at rest - where are logs stored for hosted?
[04:33] Maya: Hosted keeps logs encrypted, and you can enable extended audit logs for enterprise; Dedicated has customer-controlled storage and Private keeps logs in your VPC. We'll attach the security summary.
[04:50] Jordan: For the EU residency requirement, can hosted be region-restricted?
[04:58] Daniel: Hosted can pin region; we have EU regions and can route by policy. For strict residency you can use Private deployment.
[05:10] Priya: Ok, can you show the Console briefly - where to create API keys and view telemetry?
[05:20] Sofia: Sure, switching to Console view - Dashboard, Routes, Keys. Here's how you create a route and choose model: pick model variant, set batching policy, enable caching.
[05:40] Sofia: In Routes you can set per-route SLOs, token limits, and integrate with tracing.
[05:50] Jordan: Can we restrict keys to routes?
[05:55] Sofia: Yes, RBAC and route-scoped keys are supported. We show an example of a key with read-only or generate-only permissions.
[06:10] Daniel: Back to SDKs: environment setup - include sample .env, Dockerfile, and a small Makefile in the repo. For CI, we recommend injecting secrets via your pipeline (Vault/GCP Secret Manager/Azure Key Vault).
[06:30] Priya: Any recommended Docker base image for latency?
[06:36] Daniel: Build on a slim node/python base, enable HTTP keep-alive, and tune socket options. We have a guide in repo named 'production-tuning.md'.
[06:50] Jordan: About latency vs cost - we expect lots of short prompts, are there suggestions?
[06:58] Daniel: Use prefix caching and smaller quantized model variants; Optimize will recommend batching thresholds and quantization profiles. For short prompts, minimize batching window to hit latency SLO; Optimize can simulate cost impact.
[07:15] Priya: Do you support customer-side caching to reduce calls?
[07:20] Sofia: Yes, you can do client-side caches + platform-level prefix/KV cache. Platform cache is easiest to manage with invalidation policies.
[07:35] Ethan: From security side: encryption keys - do we bring our own keys?
[07:40] Maya: For Private and Dedicated we offer KMS integrations and optional HSM. Hosted can integrate with customer KMS for encrypting sensitive payloads.
[07:52] Daniel: Quick live demo: sample TS app that streams tokens to websocket. (code running, some typing sounds)
[08:15] Daniel: Apologies, transcript may have some mis-heard words - the package in the repo is 'redwood-client' in the example but the npm package is '@redwood/inference' - we'll make that consistent.
[08:30] Priya: That explains why we saw two names in the quickstart earlier.
[08:36] Maya: We'll push a small PR to repo to clarify naming and examples.
[08:45] Jordan: For pilot scope, we want to validate p95 latency and per-token cost over a week. Can you help with a benchmark harness?
[08:55] Daniel: Yes, we have a benchmark spreadsheet and a harness script. We'll share the link and can run an initial run with a small seed dataset.
[09:10] Priya: If we do Dedicated, what's the lead time?
[09:15] Maya: Dedicated lead time varies; for EU region typically 2-4 weeks for provisioning and validation. If it's Private on-prem, that's longer and requires security onboarding.
[09:30] Ethan: And compliance paperwork?
[09:33] Maya: We'll send SOC2 and ISO artifacts; for Private we'll do an architecture review with your security team.
[09:45] Jordan: Ok good. Any gotchas on rate limits? We have bursty traffic.
[09:50] Daniel: You can configure burst capacity and autoscale policies with Dedicated. For hosted we have soft limits and can raise them for pilots. We'll include recommended autoscale settings.
[10:05] Sofia: Dropping links: quickstart repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-quickstart, console docs: https://docs.redwood.ai/console, security brief: https://redwood.ai/security/summaries
[10:20] Priya: Thanks. A couple of nitpicks: the Docker example doesn't show pinning TLS ciphers; can you add that?
[10:28] Daniel: We'll add it.
[10:30] (short pause, some cross-talk)
[11:00] Q&A rapid fire:
[11:05] Priya: How do we do canary rollouts?
[11:10] Sofia: Console supports canary weights on routes and automatic rollback on error thresholds.
[11:20] Jordan: Can we do A/B testing with different models?
[11:25] Sofia: Yes, route-level model variants and A/B are supported; metrics are in Console.
[11:35] Ethan: For audit retention, how long is hosted retention by default?
[11:40] Maya: Default 30 days, enterprise retention add-on available. For Dedicated you control retention.
[11:50] Priya: Will you share a sample .env and Dockerfile in the Slack channel?
[11:55] Maya: Yes, will share via email and Slack.
[12:05] Action recap:
[12:10] Maya: I'll send quickstart links, pricing, and security docs. Daniel will send example code (Python/TS) and the benchmark harness. Priya will share latency targets and sample prompts.
[12:25] Jordan: Thanks everyone, that was helpful.
[12:30] End call.

Notes: transcript includes minor transcription mistakes (package names, quick corrections). References to shared artifacts: quickstart repo, console docs, security summary, benchmark spreadsheet.
